  ham bor edi).


⚠ 'PASTA' - SANALMAYDIGAN:

  ⚠ 'a pasta' - XATO.

⚠ 'GRAPES' - HAR DOIM KO'PLIKDA:

KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:

      AN APPLE.


⚠ "I'D RATHER HAVE ...":

  ⚠ "I'd rather" = 'I would rather'.
  ⚠ Keyin 'to' SIZ fe'l:
  "I'd rather HAVE" ✓

topics.topic: Grammar: Countable/Uncountable Nouns — Grammatika: Sanaladigan/sanalmaydigan otlar
topics.rule_uz:
MIQDOR SO'ZLARI - TO'LIQ TIZIM.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  SOME - TASDIQ gaplarda          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  sanalmaydigan + KO'PLIK bilan

  'There is SOME spinach left.'
  'There are SOME carrots in the

  ⚠ ISTISNO: TAKLIF va ILTIMOSda
  savolda ham 'some'!
     'Would you like SOME tea?'


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ANY - SAVOL va INKORda          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  sanalmaydigan + KO'PLIK bilan

  'Are there ANY biscuits?'
  "There isn't ANY milk."
  'Is there ANY salt?'
  "There aren't ANY potatoes."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MANY - SANALADIGAN bilan        ║
║  (savol va inkorda)              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  'How MANY eggs are there?'
  "There aren't MANY rolls left."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MUCH - SANALMAYDIGAN bilan      ║
║  (savol va inkorda)              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  'How MUCH butter is there?'
  "There isn't MUCH sugar left."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  A FEW / A LITTLE                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  A FEW + SANALADIGAN ko'plik
     'There are A FEW eggs in the
      bowl.' (some; not many)

  A LITTLE + SANALMAYDIGAN
     'There is A LITTLE coffee in
      the pot.' (some; not much)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ESLAB QOLISh JADVALI            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  SANALADIGAN (eggs):
     many, a few, some, any

  SANALMAYDIGAN (butter):
     much, a little, some, any

  ⚠ 'many butter' - XATO!
  ⚠ 'much eggs' - XATO!
  ⚠ 'a few butter' - XATO!
  ⚠ 'a little eggs' - XATO!


⚠ 'A FEW' va 'FEW':

  a few = bir nechta (IJOBIY)
  few = juda oz (SALBIY)

  ⚠ 41-betdagi maqolada 'FEW of
  these caterers' - SALBIY ma'no.


⚠ 'A LITTLE' va 'LITTLE':

  a little = biroz (IJOBIY)
  little = juda oz (SALBIY)


⚠ 'LEFT':

  'There isn't much sugar LEFT.'
  = shakar KAM QOLDI.
  ⚠ 'left' bu yerda = qolgan.
examples: We use some in affirmative sentences with uncountable nouns and plural countable nouns.
There is some spinach left. / There are some carrots in the fridge.
We use any in questions and negations with uncountable nouns and plural countable nouns.
Are there any biscuits? Yes, but there isn't any milk. / Is there any salt? Yes, but there aren't any potatoes.
We use many with countable nouns in questions and negations.
How many eggs are there? / There aren't many rolls left.
We use much with uncountable nouns in questions and negations.
How much butter is there? / There isn't much sugar left.

topics.topic: Grammar: Should/Shouldn't — Grammatika: Should/Shouldn't (1)
topics.rule_uz:
MASLAHAT BERISh - SHOULD.

║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  should + FE'L (to SIZ)
  ⚠ BARCha shaxsda bir xil:
     I/you/he/she/we/they SHOULD
  ⚠ 'He shouldS' - XATO!
  ⚠ 'should TO drink' - XATO!

  INKOR: shouldn't (= should not)
  SAVOL: Should I ...? /
         What should I do?


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MA'NOSI                         ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  should = ... qilgan ma'qul,
           ... qilish kerak (maslahat)
  shouldn't = ... qilmagan ma'qul

  'You SHOULD drink a lot of water
   daily.' (= yaxshi fikr)
  'You SHOULDN'T drink too much
   coffee.' (= yomon fikr)


⚠ 'SHOULD' va 'MUST' FARQI:

  should = MASLAHAT (bajarish
     ixtiyoriy)
  must = MAJBURIYaT (bajarish shart)

  'You should see a doctor.' -
     maslahat beraman
  'You must see a doctor.' -
     boshqa iloj yo'q


⚠ 'SHOULD' O'QILIShI:

  /ʃʊd/ - 'l' O'QILMAYDI!
  ⚠ 'shouldn't' /ˈʃʊdnt/.


⚠ 'DAILY':

  = har kuni.
  ⚠ 'every day' bilan bir xil.
  ⚠ 'weekly' (har hafta),
  'monthly' (har oy).


⚠ 'I.E.':

  = ya'ni (lotincha 'id est').
  ⚠ 'e.g.' = masalan - ADAShTIRMANG.
examples: We use should/shouldn't to give advice - i.e. to say it would be a good/bad idea for someone to do sth.
You should drink a lot of water daily. (= It's a good idea.)
You shouldn't drink too much coffee. (= It isn't a good idea.)

topics.topic: Present Perfect Simple - Form — Present Perfect Simple - shakli
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT = HAVE / HAS +
  FE'L 3-ShAKLI (V3).

  TASDIQ:
    I / you / we / they HAVE worked
    he / she / it HAS worked
    Qisqa: I've, you've, he's,
    she's, it's, we've, they've

  SO'ROQ (have/has oldinga):
    HAVE you worked?
    HAS he bought a new car?

  INKOR (not orasiga):
    I HAVEN'T worked
    He HASN'T bought a new car


V3 (PAST PARTICIPLE):

  TO'G'RI fe'llar: + -ed
    play → played, work → worked
    (V2 bilan bir xil)
  NOTO'G'RI fe'llar: alohida
    buy → bought (V2 = V3)
    see → SEEN (V2 = saw, V3 = seen)
    ⚠ Kitob oxiridagi jadval - 3-
    ustun!


⚠ 'HE'S' IKKI MA'NODA:

  he's worked = he HAS worked
  he's a doctor = he IS a doctor
  Keyin V3 bo'lsa - HAS.
examples: I have worked / I've worked — he has worked / he's worked (regular: + -ed)
I have bought / I've bought — he has bought / he's bought (irregular)
Has he bought a new car? (have/has before the subject)
He has not / hasn't bought a new car. (not between have/has and the past participle)

topics.topic: Present Perfect Simple - Use — Present Perfect Simple - ishlatilishi
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT QAChON - 4 HOLAT.

  1) NOMA'LUM VAQT (qachon - muhim
     emas, harakat muhim):
     Tom HAS BROKEN his arm.
     (qachon? - aytilmaydi; hozir
     qo'li singan)

  2) O'TMIShDA BOShLANIB, HOZIR HAM
     DAVOM ETAYOTGAN:
     Kim HAS BEEN a chef since
     1985. (hozir ham oshpaz)

  3) YAQINDA TUGAGAN, NATIJASI
     KO'RINIB TURIBDI:
     I HAVE PAINTED the kitchen.
     Doesn't it look nice?

  4) TAJRIBA (hayotda bir marta
     bo'lganmi):
     They HAVE TRAVELLED through
     Europe.


VAQT SO'ZLARI (belgilar):

  for (muddat), since (nuqta),
  just (endigina), already
  (allaqachon), yet (hali),
  lately / recently (yaqinda), so
  far (hozirgacha), ever (hech
  qachon - savolda)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Present Perfect = '-gan' / '-di'
  (natija hozir bor): 'sindirgan',
  'bo'yadim' (mana, ko'ring).
examples: Tom has broken his arm. (unstated time in the past)
Kim has been a chef since 1985. (started in the past, still continuing)
'I have painted the kitchen. Doesn't it look nice?' (recently finished, visible result)
They have travelled through Europe. (experience)
for, since, just, already, yet, lately, recently, so far, ever

topics.topic: Present Perfect - Time Words / Have gone - Have been — Present Perfect - vaqt so'zlari / Have gone - Have been
topics.rule_uz:
VAQT SO'ZLARI - QAYERDA, QAChON?

  FOR + MUDDAT (qancha vaqt):
    for ten years, for three hours
    I have known Sue FOR ten years.

  SINCE + NUQTA (qachondan):
    since 1992, since Monday
    She hasn't been to New York
    SINCE 1992.

  JUST (endigina) va ALREADY
  (allaqachon) - TASDIQDA, have va
  V3 orasida:
    She's ALREADY booked a table.
    I've JUST bought a new dress.

  YET (hali) - SAVOL va INKORDA,
  gap OXIRIDA:
    Has Jim fixed the car YET?
    They haven't cooked dinner YET.


HAVE GONE va HAVE BEEN:

  HAVE GONE TO = ketgan (hali
    o'sha yerda):
    Thomas and Anne HAVE GONE TO
    Lisbon. (hali Lissabonda)

  HAVE BEEN TO = bo'lgan (borib
    qaytgan):
    I HAVE BEEN TO Lisbon. (hozir
    bu yerdaman)
examples: I have known Sue for ten years. (for = duration)
She hasn't been to New York since 1992. (since = starting point)
She's already booked a table for two. I've just bought a new dress. (just, already - affirmative)
Has Jim fixed the car yet? They haven't cooked dinner yet. (yet - questions and negations)
Thomas and Anne have gone to Lisbon. (they are still there)
I have been to Lisbon. (I have come back)

topics.topic: Past Simple vs Present Perfect Simple — Past Simple va Present Perfect Simple farqi
topics.rule_uz:
PAST SIMPLE yoki PRESENT PERFECT?

  PAST SIMPLE - ANIQ VAQT / TUGAGAN:
    Fred GRADUATED in 1997. (qachon
    - aniq)
    Pauline WENT to the dentist
    three days ago. (ago - tugagan)

  PRESENT PERFECT - NOMA'LUM VAQT /
  HOZIR HAM DAVOM:
    Carol HAS JOINED the tennis
    club. (qachon - aytilmaydi)
    He HAS BEEN a teacher for
    twenty years. (hozir ham
    o'qituvchi)


⚠ KALIT SO'ZLAR:

  in 1997, ago, yesterday, last
  week → PAST SIMPLE
  for, since, just, already, yet,
  ever → PRESENT PERFECT


⚠ 'HE WAS A TEACHER FOR 20 YEARS'
  = endi emas (Past Simple)
  'HE HAS BEEN A TEACHER FOR 20
  YEARS' = hozir ham (Perfect)
examples: Fred graduated from university in 1997. Pauline went to the dentist three days ago. (past simple: stated time / finished)
Carol has joined the tennis club. He has been a teacher for twenty years. (present perfect: unstated time / still continuing)

topics.topic: Present Perfect Continuous
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS =
  HAVE / HAS + BEEN + FE'L-ING.

  TASDIQ: I HAVE BEEN working. She
    HAS BEEN sleeping.
  SO'ROQ: HAVE they BEEN playing?
  INKOR: She HASN'T BEEN reading.


QAChON:

  1) O'TMIShDAN HOZIRGAChA DAVOM
     (jarayon urg'ulanadi):
     She HAS BEEN TYPING letters
     FOR three hours. (hali
     yozyapti)

  2) YAQINDA TUGAGAN, NATIJASI
     KO'RINIB TURIBDI:
     They are tired. They HAVE
     BEEN WORKING for nine hours.
     (charchagan - chunki uzoq
     ishladi)


VAQT SO'ZLARI:

  for, since, all morning / all
  day / all week


⚠ SIMPLE va CONTINUOUS FARQI:

  I have painted the kitchen.
  (natija - bo'yalgan, tugadi)
  I have been painting the
  kitchen. (jarayon - shu bilan
  band edim, balki tugamagan)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  '-yapti' + 'dan beri': 'uch
  soatdan beri yozyapti'.
examples: I have been working. She has been sleeping. — Have they been playing? — She hasn't been reading.
She has been typing letters for three hours. (started in the past, continues up to the present)
They are tired. They have been working for nine hours. (recently finished, result evident now)
for, since, all morning / afternoon / week / day

topics.topic: Past Simple vs Present Perfect Simple — Past Simple va Present Perfect Simple farqi (12 (1)-mashq qoidasi)

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect — Grammatika: Present Perfect
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT - 7-UNITNING ASOSIY
GRAMMATIKASI.

╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  have/has + 3-ShAKL (past
  participle)

  I/you/we/they HAVE broken

  has; "He's tall" → is.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  TO'RT IShLATILIShI              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  1) O'TMIShDA BOShLANIB HOZIRGAChA
     DAVOM ETADI:
     'Dianne HAS BEEN in Angola FOR
      the last eight months.'
     (hali ham u yerda)

  2) YaQINDA BO'LGAN, NATIJASI
     HOZIR KO'RINIB TURIBDI:
     "I'VE BROKEN my leg, so I
      can't walk."
     (oyoq hozir singan)

  3) TAJRIBA (hayotda biror marta):
     'HAVE you ever BEEN to Angola?'

  4) VAQTI AYTILMAGAN o'tmish
     harakati - VAQT emas, HARAKAT
     muhim:
     "He'S BEEN to the dentist's
      four times."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  VAQT SO'ZLARI                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  just - hozirgina
  already - allaqachon
  yet - hali (inkor/savol)
  for - ... davomida (for 2 years)
  since - ... dan beri (since 1986)
  recently / lately - yaqinda
  so far - hozirgacha
  ever - biror marta (savol)
  never - hech qachon


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  PRESENT PERFECT va PAST SIMPLE  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  PAST SIMPLE - vaqt AYTILGAN:
     'I broke my leg LAST WEEK.'
  PRESENT PERFECT - vaqt AYTILMAGAN
  yoki hozirga bog'liq:
     "I've broken my leg." (hozir
      yura olmayman)

  ⚠ 'yesterday', 'last week', 'in
  1990', 'ago' bilan HECh QAChON
  present perfect ishlatilmaydi!


⚠ 'HAVE BEEN TO' va 'HAVE GONE TO':

  "He's BEEN to the dentist's" =
     borib QAYTGAN
  "He's GONE to the dentist's" =
     ketgan, HALI QAYTMAGAN


⚠ "THE DENTIST'S":

  = tish shifokorining (xonasi).
  ⚠ 'the dentist's', 'the doctor's',
  'the chemist's' - egalik bilan
  JOY ma'nosida.
examples: We use the present perfect to talk about an action which started in the past and continues up to the present.
Dianne has been in Angola for the last eight months.
We use it to talk about a recent action whose result is visible in the present.
I've broken my leg, so I can't walk.
We use it to talk about an experience.
Have you ever been to Angola?
We use it to talk about an action which happened at an unstated time in the past. The action is more important than the time.
He's been to the dentist's four times.

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect — Grammatika: Present Perfect (8b-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:

  Nurse: What's the problem,
         Mr Ellis?
  Patient: I've twisted my ankle.


⚠ QOLIP:

  Nurse: What's the problem, [ism]?
  Patient: I've + 3-ShAKL + my
           [tana a'zosi].


⚠ NEGA PRESENT PERFECT?

  Jarohat YaQINDA bo'lgan va NATIJASI

  2-holat).


⚠ 'MY' - TANA A'ZOSI BILAN:

  "I've twisted MY ankle"
  ⚠ Ingliz tilida tana a'zosi

⚠ 'TO BREAK ONE'S ARM':

topics.topic: Grammar: Just · Already · Yet — Grammatika: Just · Already · Yet (1)
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT BILAN UCh SO'Z.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ALREADY = allaqachon            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TASDIQ gapda, 'have' va 3-shakl
  ORASIDA:
  "I've ALREADY booked my flight."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  JUST = hozirgina                 ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TASDIQ gapda, 'have' va 3-shakl
  ORASIDA:
  "I've JUST broken the vase."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  YET = hali                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  SAVOL va INKORda, gap OXIRIDA:
  'Have you done the shopping YET?'
  "She hasn't phoned her mother YET."


⚠ O'RNI - ENG MUHIM:

  already/just → O'RTADA
     (have ___ done)
  yet → OXIRIDA
     (... done ___?)

  ⚠ "I've done it already" ham
  mumkin, lekin o'rtada odatiy.


⚠ 'YET' - TASDIQDA IShLATILMAYDI:

  ✗ "I've done it yet."
  ✓ "I've already done it."


⚠ 'TO BOOK A FLIGHT':

  = reysga chipta bron qilmoq.
  ⚠ 'to book' = bron qilmoq.


⚠ 'A VASE':

  = vaza (gul uchun).
  ⚠ Britaniyada /vɑːz/,
  AQShda /veɪs/.
examples: We use already or just in positive statements.
I've already booked my flight.
I've just broken the vase.
We use yet in questions and negations.
Have you done the shopping yet? / She hasn't phoned her mother yet.

topics.topic: Grammar: Just · Already · Yet — Grammatika: Just · Already · Yet (10b-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  'He has ALREADY made his bed.'


⚠ QOLIPLAR:

  ✓ → He has ALREADY + 3-shakl ...
  ✗ → He HASN'T + 3-shakl ... YET.


⚠ 3-ShAKLLAR:

  make → MADE
  clean → CLEANED
  put → PUT
  hang → HUNG
  remove → REMOVED
  pick up → PICKED UP


⚠ 'HIS' - EGALIK:

  'made HIS bed', 'HIS clothes' -
  ro'yxatda 'bed', 'clothes' lekin
  gapda egalik olmoshi kerak.

topics.topic: Grammar: Just · Already · Yet — Grammatika: Just · Already · Yet (11-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
TO'RT QOLIP - O'ZINGIZ HAQINGIZDA:

  I've already ......... .
  I ......... yet.
  I ......... today.
  I've just ......... .


⚠ 2-QATOR - INKOR:

  'I ... yet' → "I HAVEN'T ... yet"
  ⚠ 'yet' faqat inkor/savolda!


⚠ 3-QATOR - 'TODAY':

  'today' hali tugamagan davr →
  PRESENT PERFECT:
  "I've had lunch today."
  ⚠ Kun tugagan bo'lsa (kechqurun)
  past simple ham mumkin.

topics.topic: Grammar: Just · Already · Yet — Grammatika: Just · Already · Yet (2)
topics.rule_uz:
⚠ AUDIO KERAK - qaysi ishlar
bajarilgani faqat yozuvdan.


SAKKIZ ISh:

  paint the walls - devorlarni
     bo'yamoq
  hang the curtains - pardalarni
     osmoq
  lay the carpets - gilamlarni
     to'shamoq
  repair the back door - orqa
     eshikni ta'mirlamoq
  buy all the furniture - hamma

  mend the fence - devorni (panjara)

⚠ GAP QOLIPLARI (audiodan keyin):

  ✓ → They've already painted the
      walls.
  ✗ → They haven't hung the curtains
      yet.


⚠ 'SO FAR':

  = hozirgacha.
  ⚠ Present perfect bilan.


⚠ 'TO LAY A CARPET':

  = gilam to'shamoq.
  ⚠ lay - laid - LAID.
  ⚠ 'lie' (yotmoq) bilan
  ADAShTIRMANG.


⚠ 'TO MEND' va 'TO REPAIR':

  ⚠ 'mend' - Britaniya, oddiyroq.


⚠ 'FURNITURE':

  ⚠ SANALMAYDIGAN! 'furnitures' XATO.
  ⚠ 'a piece of furniture' ✓


⚠ 'A FENCE':

examples: paint the walls → They've already painted the walls. / They haven't painted the walls yet.
hang the curtains → hung

topics.topic: Grammar: Just · Already · Yet — Grammatika: Just · Already · Yet (3)
topics.rule_uz:
LOYIhA TOPShIRIG'I.

  ⚠ 'Photo File' - kitob oxiridagi
  bo'lim.
  ⚠ Joanne - 13-mashqdagi ayol; xat
  yangi uy haqida, present perfect
  bilan ('We've already painted
  ...').

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple (1)
topics.rule_uz:
IKKI ZAMON FARQI - ENG MUHIM MAVZU.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  PRESENT PERFECT                 ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  1) VAQTI AYTILMAGAN:
     'I HAVE BEEN to Angola.'
     (Qachon? Bilmaymiz - muhim
      emas)

  2) O'TMIShDA BOShLANIB HOZIR HAM
     DAVOM ETADI:
     'He HAS BEEN ill for a week.'
     (o'tgan hafta kasal edi va
      HALI HAM kasal)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  PAST SIMPLE                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TUGAGAN harakat, VAQTI AYTILGAN
  yoki MA'LUM:
     'He WROTE his third novel in
      1998.' (Qachon? 1998 da)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  TEZ TEKShIRUV                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  Gapda ANIQ O'TGAN VAQT bormi?
     (yesterday, last week, in 1998,
      two days ago, when I was five)
     → PAST SIMPLE

  Vaqt yo'q yoki hozirgacha davom
  etadi?
     (ever, never, just, already,
      yet, for, since, so far)
     → PRESENT PERFECT


⚠ O'ZBEKChA BILAN FARQ:

  O'zbekchada ikkalasi ham '-di' /
  '-gan' bilan ifodalanadi:
  'Angolada bo'lganman' (perfect)
  '1998 da yozdi' (past)
  ⚠ Ingliz tilida VAQT belgisi
  zamonni belgilaydi.


⚠ 'A NOVEL':

  = roman.
  ⚠ 'a novelist' = yozuvchi.
examples: We use the present perfect simple for an action which happened at an unstated time in the past or which started in the past and continues to the present.
I have been to Angola. (When? We don't know.)
He has been ill for a week. (He was ill last week and he still is.)
We use the past simple for a completed past action which happened at a stated or known time.
He wrote his third novel in 1998. (When? In 1998.)
topics.source: Coursebook, 51-bet, Present Perfect vs Past Simple qutisi

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple (2)
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  have/has + BEEN + fe'l-ING

  I HAVE BEEN WORKING
  She HAS BEEN WORKING

  ⚠ 'been' HAR DOIM - shaxsga
  qarab o'zgarmaydi.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  IKKI IShLATILIShI               ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  1) O'TMIShDA BOShLANIB HOZIR
     DAVOM ETADI - DAVOMIYLIKKA
     URG'U:
     'The organisation HAS BEEN
      SENDING medical teams since
      1986.'
     (qancha VAQT - muhim)

  2) TUGAGAN, lekin NATIJASI HOZIR
     KO'RINIB TURIBDI:
     "I'm dirty because I'VE BEEN
      WORKING in the garden."
     (kirligim - ishlaganimning
      natijasi)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  SIMPLE va CONTINUOUS FARQI      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  SIMPLE - NATIJA / SONI:
     'She HAS TREATED thousands of
      patients.' (nechta - muhim)

  CONTINUOUS - JARAYoN / QANChA
  VAQT:
     'She HAS BEEN TREATING patients
      for eight months.' (qancha
      vaqt - muhim)

  ⚠ 'How many?' → simple
  ⚠ 'How long?' → continuous


⚠ HOLAT FE'LLARI:

  know, like, love, have (egalik),
  be - continuous'da IShLATILMAYDI:
  ✗ 'I have been knowing him'
  ✓ 'I have known him for years'


⚠ 'EMPHASIS':

  = urg'u.
  ⚠ 'to give emphasis to' = urg'u
  bermoq.
examples: We use the present perfect continuous to talk about an action which started in the past and continues to the present to give emphasis to duration.
The organisation has been sending medical teams and equipment to Angola since 1986.
We also use the present perfect continuous to talk about a completed past action which has visible results in the present.
I'm dirty because I've been working in the garden.

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple (3)
topics.rule_uz:
48-BETDAGI MATNDAN.


PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS:
  has been living (in Angola)
  has been sending (medical teams)
  have been fighting (armies)
  has been working (hard)
  has been training (local people)
  have been helping (people)


PRESENT PERFECT SIMPLE:
  have grown (worse and worse)
  have become (a major problem)
  has treated (thousands of
    patients)
  has been (a meaningful experience)
  have never felt (so useful)
  has already decided (to return)


⚠ NEGA ShUNDAY?

  'has TREATED thousands' - NATIJA,
     SONI (simple)
  'has been TRAINING' - JARAYoN,
     davom etyapti (continuous)
  'has been LIVING for 8 months' -
     QANChA VAQT (continuous)
  'has BECOME a problem' - NATIJA
     (simple)

Present perfect simple: have grown, have become, has treated, has been (an experience), have never felt, has already decided

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple (17b-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
QOLIP:
  [Ega] has/have been + -ING + all

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple (4)
topics.rule_uz:
FOR va SINCE.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  FOR = DAVOMIYLIK (qancha vaqt)  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  for twenty years, for a week,
  for six months, for ages, for a
  few minutes, for two hours

  "I've been living here FOR twenty
   years."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  SINCE = BOShLANISh NUQTASI      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  since 1997, since Monday, since
  last August, since I was a child,
  since 5 o'clock

  'He has been studying English
   SINCE 1997.'


⚠ TEZ TEKShIRUV:

  'Qancha vaqt?' deb so'rasa bo'ladi
  → FOR
  'Qachondan beri?' → SINCE

  ⚠ 'since' dan keyin GAP ham kelishi
  mumkin: 'since I was a child'.


⚠ 'FOR AGES':

  = juda uzoq vaqt (so'zlashuv).
  ⚠ 'an age' = asr, davr.
examples: We use for to express duration.
I've been living here for twenty years.
We use since to state a starting point.
He has been studying English since 1997.

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple (19-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
UCh QOLIP:

  1 I've been living here for ...
    (davomiylik: five years)
  2 I've been studying English
    since ... (boshlanish: 2020)
  3 I've been ... for/since ...
    (o'zingiz tanlang)

topics.topic: Grammar: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple (20-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
'HOW LONG' SAVOLLARI.

KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  SA: How long have you been studying
      French?
  SB: I've been studying French for
      seven years.


⚠ SAVOL QOLIPI:

  How long have you been + -ING ...?
  ⚠ 'How long' = qancha vaqtdan beri.


⚠ JAVOBDA for/since:

  Seven years → FOR seven years
  Last August → SINCE last August
  1982 → SINCE 1982
  a few minutes → FOR a few minutes
  last month → SINCE last month
  two hours → FOR two hours


⚠ 'TO SUNBATHE':

  = quyoshda toblanmoq.
  ⚠ 'sun' + 'bathe' (cho'milmoq).


⚠ 'RACING CARS':

  = poyga mashinalari.
  ⚠ 'to drive racing cars' = poyga
  mashinasi haydamoq.

topics.topic: Grammar — Grammatika (7-mashq qoidasi) (3)
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT - HAYOT TAJRIBASI
  (coursebook 49-bet qoidasi).

  SAVOL: Have you EVER + V3?
    = hech qachon ... misiz?
  HA: I've + V3.
  YO'Q: I've NEVER + V3.

  ⚠ 'ever' faqat SAVOLDA, 'never'
  javobda (inkor bilan EMAS).


V3 ShAKLLARI:

  have → HAD
  break → BROKEN
  twist → TWISTED


⚠ 'THE FLU':

  = gripp ('the' bilan).


⚠ 'MEASLES':

  = qizamiq. '-s' bilan tugasa
  ham BIRLIK.


⚠ 'A TROPICAL DISEASE':

  = tropik kasallik (bezgak
  kabi).


⚠ 'TO TWIST YOUR ANKLE':

  = to'piqni chiqarib olmoq
  (= sprain).


⚠ 'A MEDICAL SURVEY':

  = tibbiy so'rovnoma.

topics.topic: Grammar — Grammatika (9-mashq qoidasi) (5)
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT vs PAST SIMPLE
  (coursebook 50-bet qoidasi).

  PRESENT PERFECT - natija HOZIR,
  vaqt AYTILMAGAN:
    'I've hurt my arm' (hozir
    og'riyapti)
    'Have you seen a doctor yet?'
    'I haven't broken any bones'
    'I've never injured myself'
  PAST SIMPLE - ANIQ O'TGAN VAQT:
    'when did you do that?' (when)
    'I did it yesterday'
    'it hurt when it happened'
    'I went last night'

  ⚠ 'when', 'yesterday', 'last
  night' → PAST SIMPLE.
  ⚠ 'yet', 'never', vaqtsiz →
  PRESENT PERFECT.


⚠ 'WHAT'S THE MATTER?':

  = Nima bo'ldi? (= What's wrong?)


⚠ 'PAINFUL':

  = og'riqli.


⚠ 'TO INJURE ONESELF':

  = o'zini jarohatlamoq.


⚠ 'BESIDES':

  = bundan tashqari.


⚠ 'FOR A WHILE':

  = bir muddat.

topics.topic: Grammar — Grammatika (11b-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
PRESENT PERFECT + SINCE/FOR.

  QOLIP: X has/have + V3 + ... +
  for/since ...

  ⚠ O'tmishda boshlanib HOZIRGAChA
  davom etayotgan holat.

topics.topic: Past Perfect Simple — Past Perfect Simple (o'tgan tugallangan zamon) (1)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST PERFECT = HAD + V3 (hamma
  shaxsda bir xil!).

  TASDIQ: I / he / they HAD bought
    Qisqa: I'd, he'd, they'd
    I HAD CLEANED my room.
  SO'ROQ: HAD he arrived? HAD they
    bought a car?
  INKOR: He HADN'T watered the
    plants.
  QISQA JAVOB: Yes, he had. / No,
    he hadn't.


⚠ 'HE'D' IKKI MA'NODA:

  he'd bought = he HAD bought
  he'd like = he WOULD like
  Keyin V3 bo'lsa - HAD.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  '-gan edi': 'tozalagan edim',
  'sotib olgan edi'.
examples: I had bought / I'd bought — he had bought / he'd bought (same for all persons)
I had cleaned my room. (had + past participle)
Had he arrived? Had they bought a car? (had before the subject)
He hadn't watered the plants. They hadn't won a prize. (not after had)
Had he bought ...? — Yes, he had. / No, he hadn't.

topics.topic: Past Perfect Simple — Past Perfect Simple (o'tgan tugallangan zamon) (2)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST PERFECT QAChON:

  1) O'TMIShDA IKKI HARAKAT -
     OLDINGISI:
     OLDIN → Past Perfect (had V3)
     KEYIN → Past Simple (V2)
     They HAD BOOKED a room before
     they WENT on holiday.
     (avval band qildi, keyin
     ketdi)

  2) PRESENT PERFECT NING O'TMIShI:
     Greg ISN'T at home. He HAS
     GONE out. (hozir yo'q)
     Greg WASN'T at home. He HAD
     GONE out. (o'shanda yo'q edi)


VAQT SO'ZLARI:

  already, by the time (... gacha),
  never, as soon as, just, after,
  when, before


PAST CONTINUOUS va PAST PERFECT:

  CONTINUOUS - davom etayotgan
    harakat UZILDI:
    He WAS WATCHING TV when the
    phone RANG. (bir vaqtda)

  PERFECT - bir harakat ikkinchi-
    sidan OLDIN TUGADI:
    They HAD BOOKED a room before
    they WENT. (ketma-ket)


⚠ 'BY THE TIME':

  = ... vaqtiga kelib, ... gacha.
examples: The action which happened earlier → past perfect; the action which happened later → past simple.
Greg wasn't at home. He had gone out. (Greg was out then.)
Greg isn't at home. He has gone out. (Greg is out now.)
already, by the time, never, as soon as, just, after, when, before
He was watching TV when the phone rang. (past continuous: in progress, interrupted)
They had booked a room before they went on holiday. (past perfect: before another past action)
topics.source: Grammar 2, 40-bet (Past Perfect - Use / Past Continuous vs Past Perfect)

topics.topic: Grammar: Past Perfect Simple — Grammatika: Past Perfect Simple (1)
topics.rule_uz:
PAST PERFECT - 8-UNITNING ASOSIY
GRAMMATIKASI.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  HAD + 3-ShAKL (past participle)
  ⚠ BARCha shaxsda 'had' - o'zgarmaydi!

  TASDIQ: I/he/they HAD eaten
  INKOR: HADN'T eaten (had not)
  SAVOL: HAD you eaten?
  QISQA JAVOB: Yes, I had. /
     No, I hadn't.

  QISQARTMA: I'd, he'd, they'd
  ⚠ "I'd" = 'I had' (past perfect)
  yoki 'I would' - kontekstga qarab:
  "I'd eaten" → had; "I'd like" →
  would.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  IShLATILIShI                    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  O'TMIShDA IKKI VOQEA - qaysi biri
  OLDIN bo'lganini ko'rsatadi:

  'He called Jane AFTER he HAD
   FINISHED dinner.'
  1-voqea: finished dinner (past
     perfect - OLDINGISI)
  2-voqea: called Jane (past
     simple - KEYINGISI)

  ⚠ "O'tmishdan ham oldingi o'tmish"
  deb eslab qoling.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  PRESENT PERFECT BILAN ALOQASI   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  present perfect: has/have + 3-shakl
     'He HAS never travelled abroad.'
     (hozirgacha)
  past perfect: had + 3-shakl
     'He HAD never travelled abroad.'
     (o'tmishdagi biror paytgacha)

  ⚠ Past perfect = present perfect
  ning O'TGAN ZAMONI.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  VAQT SO'ZLARI                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  already, by the time, never,
  as soon as, just, after, when,
  before

  ⚠ 'by the time' = ... gacha,
  ... paytga kelib.
  ⚠ 'as soon as' = ... zahoti.


⚠ 'BEFORE' va 'AFTER' BILAN:

  'AFTER he HAD finished, he
   called.' (after + past perfect)
  'BEFORE he called, he HAD
   finished.' (before + past simple,
   asosiy gap past perfect)


⚠ 'EQUIVALENT':

  = ekvivalent, teng.
  ⚠ 'the past equivalent of' =
  ... ning o'tgan zamondagi tengi.
examples: When he reached the beach, he told the tourists what had happened.
We form the past perfect simple with had + the past participle of the main verb.
Affirmative: I/you/he/she/it/we/you/they had eaten. Negative: had not / hadn't eaten. Interrogative: Had I/you/... eaten? Short answers: Yes, I had. / No, I hadn't.
We use the past perfect simple to talk about a past action which happened before another past action.
He called Jane after he had finished dinner. (First he finished dinner, then he called Jane.)
The past perfect simple is the past equivalent of the present perfect simple.
He has never travelled abroad. (present perfect simple) / He had never travelled abroad. (past perfect simple)
Time expressions used with the past perfect: already, by the time, never, as soon as, just, after, when, before etc.

topics.topic: The Passive - Form — Majhul nisbat - shakli
topics.rule_uz:
MAJHUL NISBAT = TO BE + V3.

  Zamon 'TO BE' ORQALI ko'rsatiladi,
  V3 o'zgarmaydi:

  PRESENT SIMPLE:  is / are + V3
    The dog IS FED twice a day.
  PAST SIMPLE:     was / were + V3
    The dog WAS FED yesterday.
  PRESENT PERFECT: has / have BEEN
    + V3
    The dog HAS BEEN FED.
  FUTURE:          will BE + V3
    The dog WILL BE FED.
  MODAL:           should BE + V3
    The dog SHOULD BE FED.

  SAVOL: IS this car made in Japan?
  INKOR: His bicycle WASN'T stolen.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Majhul = '-il' / '-in' qo'shimchasi:
  boqadi → boqILadi; yozdi →
  yozILdi; o'g'irladi → o'g'irLANdi.
examples: He feeds the dog twice a day. → The dog is fed twice a day. (present simple)
He fed the dog yesterday. → The dog was fed yesterday. (past simple)
He has fed the dog. → The dog has been fed. (present perfect)
He will feed the dog. → The dog will be fed. (future simple)
He should feed the dog. → The dog should be fed. (modal)
Is this car made in Japan? — His bicycle wasn't stolen last night.

topics.topic: Turning from Active into Passive — Faoldan majhulga o'tkazish
topics.rule_uz:
FAOL → MAJHUL - 3 QADAM.

  FAOL:   Susan  made      a cake.
          (ega)  (fe'l)    (to'ld.)
             ↘            ↙
  MAJHUL: A cake was made by Susan.
          (ega)  (majhul)  (bajaruvchi)

  a) To'ldiruvchi → ega
  b) Fe'l → to be + V3
  c) Ega → by + bajaruvchi


QOIDALAR:

  1) FAQAT TO'LDIRUVChILI fe'llar:
     Tom watered THE PLANTS. →
     The plants were watered.
     ⚠ 'It is raining' → majhul
     YO'Q (to'ldiruvchi yo'q).

  2) BAJARUVChI TUShADI (someone,
     people, they):
     Someone will feed the dog. →
     The dog will be fed. ('by
     someone' yozilmaydi)

  3) TUShUM OLMOSh → EGA OLMOSh:
     She gave ME money. → I was
     given money.

  4) PREDLOG SAQLANADI:
     Someone broke INTO our house.
     → Our house was broken INTO.
examples: ACTIVE: Susan made a cake. → PASSIVE: A cake was made by Susan.
Tom watered the plants. → The plants were watered by Tom. But: It is raining today. (no object - no passive)
Someone will feed the dog. → The dog will be fed. (agent omitted)
She gave me some money. → I was given some money. (object pronoun → subject pronoun)
Someone broke into our house last night. → Our house was broken into last night. (preposition kept)

topics.rule_uz:
MAJHUL NISBAT - 9-UNITNING ASOSIY
GRAMMATIKASI.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TO BE (kerakli zamonda) + 3-ShAKL

  Present Simple:  am/is/are + taken
  Past Simple:     was/were + carried
  Present Perfect: has/have been +
                   mined
  Future:          will be + amazed
  Modal:           can/should be +
                   seen

  ⚠ Zamonni 'BE' ko'rsatadi, asosiy
  fe'l HAR DOIM 3-shaklda.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ACTIVE → PASSIVE                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  ACTIVE:  Fire destroyed a chapel.
           (ega)  (fe'l)  (to'ldiruvchi)
  PASSIVE: A chapel was destroyed
           by fire.
           (ega)    (fe'l)   (agent)

  1) Active to'ldiruvchisi →
     passive egasi
  2) Fe'l → be + 3-shakl (zamon
     saqlanadi)
  3) Active egasi → 'by' + agent
     (yoki tushiriladi)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  QAChON IShLATILADI              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  HARAKAT muhim, KIM qilgani muhim
  emas yoki noma'lum:

  'Salt WAS DISCOVERED.'
  (kim topgani muhim emas)

  ⚠ 'by' + agent faqat agent MUHIM
  bo'lganda: 'was destroyed BY FIRE'.


⚠ 8b JAVOBI - AGENTSIZ GAPLAR:

  'Visitors are taken down' - kim
     olib tushishi muhim emas
  'Salt has been mined there' -
     konchilar - aniq, aytish shart
     emas
  ⚠ Agent NOMA'LUM, AhAMIYaTSIZ yoki
  ANIQ bo'lsa tushiriladi.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA BILAN:

  Majhul nisbat o'zbekchada '-il/-in'
  bilan: 'topildi', 'qurilgan',
  'olib tushiladi'.


⚠ 'AN AGENT':

  = harakatni bajaruvchi.
  ⚠ 'the appropriate tense' = mos
  zamon.
examples: They take visitors down into a hidden world. → Visitors are taken down into a hidden world.
The miners carried salt up to the surface. → Salt was carried up to the surface by the miners.
They have mined salt there for over 700 years. → Salt has been mined there for over 700 years.
These unforgettable sights will amaze you. → You will be amazed by these unforgettable sights.
To form the passive, we use the appropriate tense of the verb to be + the past participle of the main verb.
We use the passive when the action is more important than the agent. Salt was discovered.
Active: Fire (subject) destroyed (verb) a chapel in 1697 (object). Passive: A chapel (subject) was destroyed (verb) by fire in 1697 (agent).

topics.topic: Must - Have to — Must - Have to (majburiyat)
topics.rule_uz:
MUST / HAVE TO - KERAK, MAJBUR.

  MUST - so'zlovchining fikri /
    kuchli maslahat:
    You MUST stay in bed.
    You MUST see a doctor right
    away.

  HAVE TO - tashqi majburiyat
    (qoida, holat):
    I HAVE TO go to the post
    office.

  ⚠ MUST faqat HOZIRGI zamon.
  Boshqa zamonlar HAVE TO bilan:
    I'LL HAVE TO work on Saturday.
    She HAD TO stay in bed.


INKORLAR - MA'NOSI BUTUNLAY
  BOShQA!

  MUSTN'T = TAQIQ (qilma!):
    You MUSTN'T park here. (qoidaga
    zid)
    You MUSTN'T eat too many
    sweets.

  DON'T HAVE TO = ShART EMAS
    (xohlasang qil):
    You DON'T HAVE TO buy oranges.
    We've got plenty.


O'TGAN ZAMON:

  had to - majbur edim:
    I HAD TO walk to school!
  didn't have to - shart emas edi:
    We DIDN'T HAVE TO learn a
    foreign language.


⚠ 'RIGHT AWAY':

  = darhol.


⚠ 'PLENTY':

  = ko'p, yetarlicha.
examples: You must stay in bed. I have to go to the post office. (obligation, necessity)

You must see a doctor right away. You mustn't eat too many sweets. (strong advice)
You mustn't park here. (prohibition = You aren't allowed to)
You don't have to buy any oranges. We've got plenty. (lack of necessity)

    bog'liq emas):
    AM I ALLOWED TO park my
    motorcycle here? (qonun nima
    deydi?)
    You AREN'T ALLOWED TO take
    photographs in the museum.


COULD / COULDN'T - O'TGAN ZAMON:

  I COULD go to bed late when I
  was 17 but I COULDN'T drink
  wine.
  (mumkin edi / mumkin emas edi)


⚠ 'TO TAKE PICTURES / PHOTOGRAPHS':

  = suratga olmoq.
examples: 'Can I watch TV?' 'Of course, you can.' I'm afraid you can't take pictures. (permission - speaker)
Am I allowed to park my motorcycle here? You aren't allowed to take photographs in the museum. (permission - rules/law)
I could go to bed late when I was 17 but I couldn't drink wine. (past of can/can't)

topics.topic: Grammar: Imperative / Reflexive Pronouns — Grammatika: Buyruq mayli / O'zlik olmoshlari (1)
topics.rule_uz:
BUYRUQ MAYLI (THE IMPERATIVE).


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TASDIQ: fe'lning ASOSIY shakli
     (ega YO'Q):
     'Put a fence around any ponds.'
     'Keep cleaning products in a
      safe place.'

  INKOR: DON'T + fe'l:
     "Don't let your children play
      with matches."
  ⚠ 'NEVER' + fe'l - kuchli inkor:
     'Never allow ...'


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  IShLATILIShI                    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  Odamlarga NIMA QILISh / QILMASLIKNI
  aytish: buyruq, ko'rsatma,
  ogohlantirish, maslahat, taklif.

  ⚠ 'Please' bilan muloyimroq:
  'Please close the door.'


⚠ 'YOU' AYTILMAYDI:

  ✗ 'You put a fence.'
  ✓ 'Put a fence.'


⚠ 'ALWAYS' va 'NEVER' BILAN:

  'ALWAYS put knives away.'
  'NEVER let children play with
   matches.'
examples: We use the imperative to tell people what to do/not to do.
Put a fence around any ponds in your garden.
Don't let your children play with matches.

topics.topic: Grammar: Imperative / Reflexive Pronouns — Grammatika: Buyruq mayli / O'zlik olmoshlari (2)
topics.rule_uz:
VARAQADAGI BUYRUQ ShAKLLARI:

  Read this leaflet
  make sure
  Keep all cleaning products
  Always put knives ... away
  Never allow your children
  Make sure you cover
  Never let your children play
  Fit safety gates
  Put a fence

  ⚠ To'qqizta buyruq.
  ⚠ 'Never allow', 'Never let' -
  inkor buyruqlar.
examples: Read, make sure, Keep, put (away), Never allow, Make sure, Never let, Fit, Put

topics.topic: Grammar: Imperative / Reflexive Pronouns — Grammatika: Buyruq mayli / O'zlik olmoshlari (3)
topics.rule_uz:
O'ZLIK OLMOShLARI (REFLEXIVE
PRONOUNS).


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLLARI                       ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  I     → myself
  you   → yourself (birlik)
  he    → himself
  she   → herself
  it    → itself
  we    → ourselves
  you   → yourselves (ko'plik)
  they  → themselves

  ⚠ Birlik '-self', ko'plik
  '-selves'.
  ⚠ 'hisself', 'theirselves' - XATO!


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  IShLATILIShI                    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  EGA va TO'LDIRUVChI BIR ODAM/NARSA
  bo'lganda:

  'They might cut THEMSELVES.'
  (ular o'zlarini kesadi)

  ⚠ Taqqoslang:
  'He hurt HIMSELF.' - o'zini
  'He hurt HIM.' - boshqa odamni


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  'o'zim, o'zing, o'zi, o'zimiz,
  o'zingiz, o'zlari'.


⚠ 'ENJOY YOURSELF':

  = yaxshi dam olmoq, zavqlanmoq.
  ⚠ 'enjoy' dan keyin to'ldiruvchi
  ShART: 'They enjoyed themselves.'
examples: We use reflexive pronouns when the subject and the object of the verb refer to the same person or thing.
They might cut themselves.

topics.topic: Grammar: Might/Could — Grammatika: Might/Could (1)
topics.rule_uz:
MIGHT va COULD - EhTIMOL.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MA'NOSI                         ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = ... bo'lishi MUMKIN (ehtimol).
  'Stay away from the dog. It
   MIGHT/COULD bite you.'
  (tishlashi mumkin - aniq emas)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  might/could + FE'L (to SIZ)
  ⚠ Barcha shaxsda bir xil.
  ⚠ 'might to bite' - XATO!

  INKOR: might not (mightn't) /
     could not (couldn't)


⚠ 'MIGHT' va 'MAY':

  Ikkalasi ehtimol; 'may' biroz
  kuchliroq (50%), 'might' kamroq
  (30%).


⚠ 'COULD' - IKKI MA'NO:

  1) ehtimol: 'It could rain.'
  2) o'tmishdagi 'can': 'I could
     swim when I was five.'
  ⚠ Kontekst ochib beradi.


⚠ 'STAY AWAY FROM':

  = ... dan uzoq turmoq.
examples: We use might or could to say that it is possible that something will happen.
Stay away from the dog. It might/could bite you.

topics.topic: Grammar: Might/Could — Grammatika: Might/Could (9b-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
QOLIP:
  [Ism] might/could + fe'l ...

topics.topic: Grammar: Might/Could — Grammatika: Might/Could (10b-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:

  SA: Never play with burning
      candles.
  SB: Why?
  SA: You might start a fire.


⚠ QOLIP:

  ✗ → Never + fe'l. Why? You
     might/could ...
  ✓ → Always + fe'l. Why? It
     might/could ...

topics.topic: Grammar: Might/Could — Grammatika: Might/Could (2)
topics.rule_uz:
LOYIhA TOPShIRIG'I.

⚠ NAMUNA VARAQA:

  FIRE PRECAUTIONS
  • Never play with burning candles.
    You might start a fire.
  • Never smoke in bed. You could
    fall asleep and set the house on
    fire.
  • Always be careful when cooking

examples: Never play with burning candles. You might start a fire.
Never smoke in bed. You could fall asleep and set the house on fire.
Always be careful when cooking with hot oil. It might catch fire.
Make sure you fit a smoke alarm. It could warn you of a fire in your house.
Always have a fire extinguisher in your house. You might stop a small fire.

topics.topic: Grammar: Have to / Must — Grammatika: Have to / Must (1)
topics.rule_uz:
MAJBURIYaT VA TAQIQ.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  HAVE TO = ZARURAT               ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  'You HAVE TO buy a ticket before
   getting on the train.'
  ⚠ Tashqi qoida, zarurat.
  ⚠ he/she/it → HAS TO.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  DON'T HAVE TO = ShART EMAS      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  "You DON'T HAVE TO help me wash
   the car." (xohlasang - qilasan)
  ⚠ TAQIQ EMAS! Faqat 'kerak emas'.
  ⚠ he/she → DOESN'T HAVE TO.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MUST = JUDA KUChLI MASLAHAT     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  'You MUST stay away from the
   boats.' (juda muhim)
  ⚠ Gapiruvchining O'Z fikri.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MUSTN'T = TAQIQ                 ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  "You MUSTN'T go near the rocks."
  (juda muhim - bormaslik)
  "You MUSTN'T steal." (qonun
   taqiqlaydi)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ENG KATTA XATO                  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  DON'T HAVE TO ≠ MUSTN'T

  "You don't have to come." =
     kelishing shart emas (xohlasang
     kel)
  "You mustn't come." = kelma!
     (taqiq)

  ⚠ O'zbekchada ikkalasi ham 'kerak
  emas' deb tarjima qilinishi
  mumkin - DIQQAT!


⚠ 'MUST' O'TGAN ZAMONI YO'Q:

  → 'had to' ishlatiladi.
  'I HAD TO buy a ticket yesterday.'


⚠ 'ILLEGAL':

  = noqonuniy.
  ⚠ 'legal' = qonuniy.


⚠ 'PROHIBITION':

  = taqiq.
examples: We use have to to express necessity. You have to buy a ticket before getting on the train.
We use do not have to to say that it is not necessary for something to happen. You don't have to help me wash the car. (... but you can if you want to.)
We can use must/mustn't to express very strong advice. You must stay away from the boats. You mustn't go near the rocks.
We also use mustn't to express prohibition. You mustn't steal from other people. (It's illegal.)

topics.topic: Grammar: Have to / Must — Grammatika: Have to / Must (2)
topics.rule_uz:
⚠ AUDIO KERAK - jadval yozuvdan
to'ldiriladi. Birinchi qator kitobda
tayyor.

KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  'Chris HAS TO get up early to catch

JADVAL 'Who has to ...':

  get up early to catch the school

  stay in the school grounds at

  go to lessons on Saturday

  clean the classroom? - ?


⚠ GAP QOLIPLARI:

  ✗ → [Ism] DOESN'T HAVE TO ...

  'Anne doesn't have to get up early

⚠ 'A BOARDING SCHOOL':

  yashaydi).


⚠ 'HIGH SCHOOL':

  = o'rta maktab (AQSh, 14-18 yosh).


⚠ 'SCHOOL GROUNDS':

examples: Chris has to get up early to catch the school bus. Anne doesn't have to get up early to catch the school bus.
wear a school uniform?
stay in the school grounds at lunchtime?
go to lessons on Saturday mornings?
clean the classroom?

topics.topic: Grammar: Have to / Must — Grammatika: Have to / Must (12-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  'You MUST keep all cleaning

  buyruq (inkor: Never) → You

⚠ 'MUSTN'T' O'QILIShI:

topics.topic: Grammar: must / mustn't / don't have to — Grammatika: must / mustn't / don't have to (13-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
O'Z MAMLAKATINGIZ HAQIDA -
"to'g'ri" javob yo'q.

KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  "In my country, taxi drivers don't
   have to wear a uniform."


UCh USTUN:

  must = ShART (qoida)
  mustn't = TAQIQ
  don't have to = ShART EMAS


EhTIMOLIY JAVOBLAR (O'zbekiston):

  wear a uniform → don't have to
  switch the meter on → must
  drive carefully → must
  be rude to passengers → mustn't
  carry more than four passengers →
     mustn't
  have a mobile phone with them →
     don't have to


⚠ 'TO SWITCH ON':

  = yoqmoq (asbob).
  ⚠ 'the meter' = taksometr.


⚠ 'A PASSENGER':

  = yo'lovchi.
  ⚠ O'qilishi /ˈpæsɪndʒə/.


⚠ 'RUDE TO SB':

  = kimgadir qo'pol.

topics.topic: Grammar: Can - Be allowed to — Grammatika: Can - Be allowed to
topics.rule_uz:
RUXSAT: CAN va BE ALLOWED TO.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  CAN / CAN'T                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  Ruxsat SO'RASh, BERISh, RAD ETISh:
  "Can I go out?" - "Of course you
   can."
  "I'm afraid you can't enter this
   room."
  ⚠ Ruxsat GAPIRUVChIga bog'liq.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  BE ALLOWED TO                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = ruxsat berilgan bo'lmoq.
  ⚠ Ruxsat QOIDAga bog'liq,
  gapiruvchiga EMAS.

  'Can I play in the garden?'
     = Sen menga ruxsat berasanmi?
  'Am I allowed to use the
   telephone?'
     = Qoida bo'yicha mumkinmi?


⚠ ShAKLI:

  am/is/are + allowed to + fe'l
  'You aren't allowed to park here.'
  'Are we allowed to smoke?'


⚠ 'TO ALLOW':

  = ruxsat bermoq.
  ⚠ 'allow sb TO do' (70-bet).


⚠ 'PERMISSION':

  = ruxsat (ot).
  ⚠ 'to ask for permission' = ruxsat
  so'ramoq.
examples: We use can to ask for or give permission, and can't to refuse permission. "Can I go out?" "Of course you can." I'm afraid you can't enter this room.
We use be allowed to to ask for, give or refuse permission. The permission, however, does not depend on the speaker.
Can I play in the garden? (Will you allow me to play in the garden?) / Am I allowed to use the telephone? (What is the rule?)

topics.topic: Grammar: Can - Be allowed to — Grammatika: Can - Be allowed to (14-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:

  SA: Can I park my car here?
  SB: No, I'm afraid not. You aren't
      allowed to park here. You have
      to park somewhere else.


⚠ QOLIP:

  SA: Can [ega] + fe'l ...?
  SB: No, I'm afraid not. [Ega]
      aren't/isn't allowed to ...
      [Ega] have/has to [qavsdagi].


⚠ 'A CLOAKROOM':

  = garderob (kiyim, sumka
  qoldiriladigan joy).


⚠ 'A SUIT AND TIE':

  = kostyum va galstuk.


⚠ 'A PUBLIC PHONE':

  = jamoat telefoni (taksofon).

topics.topic: Grammar: Had to / Could — Grammatika: Had to / Could (1)
topics.rule_uz:
O'TGAN ZAMONDA MAJBURIYaT VA RUXSAT.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  HAD TO / DIDN'T HAVE TO         ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = 'have to' / 'don't have to'
  ning O'TGAN ZAMONI.

  'When my father was a boy, he HAD
   TO wear shorts to school.'
  "Children DIDN'T HAVE TO learn
   about computers twenty years
   ago."

  ⚠ 'must' ning o'tgan zamoni YO'Q -
  'had to' ishlatiladi!


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  COULD / COULDN'T                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = 'can' / 'can't' ning O'TGAN
  ZAMONI (ruxsat, imkoniyat).

  'I COULD go to parties when I was
   17, but I COULDN'T go on my own;
   I HAD TO go with my brother.'


⚠ SAVOL ShAKLLARI:

  DID you HAVE TO ...?
  COULD you ...?


⚠ 'ON MY OWN':

  = yolg'iz o'zim.
  ⚠ 'by myself' bilan bir xil.


⚠ 'TWENTY YEARS AGO':

  = yigirma yil oldin.
  ⚠ 'ago' - vaqtdan KEYIN.
examples: Had to and didn't have to are the past forms of have to and don't have to.
When my father was a boy, he had to wear shorts to school. Children didn't have to learn about computers at school twenty years ago.
Could and couldn't are the past forms of can and can't.
I could go to parties when I was 17, but I couldn't go on my own; I had to go with my brother.

topics.topic: Grammar: Had to / Could — Grammatika: Had to / Could (2)
topics.rule_uz:
⚠ AUDIO KERAK - jadval yozuvdan
to'ldiriladi.


JADVAL (could / couldn't / had to /
didn't have to):

  wear best clothes - HAD TO
     (namunada tayyor)
  play piano for guests before
     dinner - ?
  cook - ?
  sit at same table as adults - ?
  put elbows on table - ?
  drink wine like adults - ?
  go to bed early - ?
  sit in living room with adults
     after dinner - ?


⚠ EhTIMOLIY (eski davr qoidalari):

  cook → didn't have to
  sit at same table → couldn't
  put elbows on table → couldn't
  drink wine → couldn't
  go to bed early → had to
  ⚠ Audio bilan tekshiring!


⚠ 'A DINNER PARTY':

  = kechki ziyofat (uyda).


⚠ 'ELBOWS':

  = tirsaklar.
  ⚠ 'Don't put your elbows on the
  table!' - odob qoidasi.


⚠ 'A GRANDDAUGHTER':

  = nabira (qiz).
examples: wear best clothes → had to
play piano for guests before dinner
cook
sit at same table as adults
put elbows on table
drink wine like adults
go to bed early
sit in living room with adults after dinner

topics.topic: Grammar: Had to / Could — Grammatika: Had to / Could (15b-mashq qoidasi)
topics.rule_uz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:

  SA: Did they have to wear their
      best clothes?
  SB: Yes, they did. They had to
      wear their best clothes.


⚠ SAVOL VA JAVOB QOLIPLARI:

  Did they have to ...?
     Yes, they did. / No, they
     didn't. They didn't have to ...
  Could they ...?
     Yes, they could. / No, they
     couldn't.

⚠ Javoblar audioga bog'liq -
qoliplar berilgan.

topics.topic: Grammar — Grammatika (5-mashq qoidasi) (2)
topics.rule_uz:
MUST / MUSTN'T (coursebook 72-bet
  qoidasi).

  MUST = shart, majburiy (qilish
    kerak)
  MUSTN'T = taqiqlangan (qilish
    MUMKIN EMAS)

  ⚠ 'mustn't' ≠ 'don't have to'!
  mustn't = taqiq
  don't have to = shart emas

  1 mustn't be late (kech qolma)
  2 must pay (to'lash shart)
  3 mustn't bring (taqiq)
  4 mustn't forget (unutma)
  5 must phone (shart)
  6 mustn't eat (taqiq - tishlar)
  7 must be at the airport (shart)
  8 must wear a helmet (shart)
  9 mustn't be late (kech
    qolmaylik)
  10 must tidy (shart)


⚠ 'THE RENT':

  = ijara haqi.


⚠ 'A HELMET':

  = dubulg'a, kaska.


⚠ 'BY EIGHT O'CLOCK':

  = sakkizgacha.

topics.topic: Grammar — Grammatika (8-mashq qoidasi) (4)
topics.rule_uz:
O'ZLIK OLMOShLARI (coursebook
  71-bet qoida-o'zlik).

  IKKI VAZIFA:
  1) Ega = to'ldiruvchi:
     'hurt yourself', 'scalded
     myself', 'cut himself'
  2) 'O'ZI' (urg'u - yordamsiz):
     'I can do it MYSELF', 'I made
     it MYSELF', 'he fixed it
     HIMSELF', 'they painted it
     THEMSELVES', 'my mother made
     it HERSELF'

  1 you → yourself
  2 I → myself
  3 I → myself
  4 he → himself
  5 I → myself
  6 he → himself
  7 they → themselves
  8 my mother → herself


⚠ 'THE ROBINSONS':

  = Robinsonlar oilasi → they.

topics.topic: Grammar — Grammatika (10-mashq qoidasi) (4)
topics.rule_uz:
COULD / COULDN'T - O'TGAN ZAMON
  QOBILIYATI.

  could = qila olardim
  couldn't = qila olmasdim

  ⚠ 'can' ning o'tgan zamoni =
  'could'.
  ⚠ 'could' dan keyin fe'l ODDIY
  ShAKLDA.


QOLIP:
  When I was five, I could ... and
  ..., but I couldn't ... or ... .

  ⚠ Inkorda 'or': 'I couldn't play
  tennis OR speak English'.

topics.topic: Conditionals Type 2 — 2-tur shart gap
topics.rule_uz:
2-TUR ShART GAP - XAYOLIY VAZIYAT.

  IF + PAST SIMPLE, + WOULD /
  COULD / MIGHT + FE'L

  If I HAD more free time, I WOULD
  TAKE UP basketball.
  (aslida vaqtim yo'q - xayol)

  ⚠ 'if' qismida O'TGAN ZAMON,
  lekin ma'no HOZIR/KELAJAK!
  ⚠ 'would' dan keyin fe'l ASOSIY
  shaklda.


1-TUR bilan FARQI:

  1-tur: If I HAVE time, I WILL
    go. (real - balki boradi)
  2-tur: If I HAD time, I WOULD
    go. (xayoliy - vaqtim yo'q)


WERE - HAMMA ShAXSDA:

  If I WERE rich, I would travel
  around the world.
  (If I was rich - og'zaki nutqda
  ham mumkin)


MASLAHAT - IF I WERE YOU:

  IF I WERE YOU, I would stop
  eating junk food.
  (Sening o'rningda bo'lsam ...)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  '-sa edi ... -ardi':
  'boy bo'lsam edi, sayohat
  qilardim'.


⚠ 'TO TAKE UP':

  = (yangi mashg'ulot) boshlamoq.
examples: If + past simple → would/could/might + bare infinitive
If I had more free time, I would take up basketball. (improbable situation)
If I were rich, I would travel around the world. (were for all persons)
If I were you, I would stop eating junk food. (advice)

topics.topic: Conditionals Type 2 — 2-tur shart gap (7-mashq qoidasi)

2-TUR ShART GAPLARI - 11-UNITNING
ASOSIY GRAMMATIKASI.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  IF + PAST SIMPLE,
  WOULD/COULD/MIGHT + FE'L (to siz)

   NOT ALLOW hunters ...'

╔══════════════════════════════════╗

╚══════════════════════════════════╝

║  1-TUR va 2-TUR FARQI            ║

  1-TUR (real):

  2-TUR (xayoliy):

║  'WERE' - HAMMA ShAXSDA          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  'If he WERE rich ...'

  not.

topics.rule_uz:
⚠ 'GREEN' bu yerda = tabiatni
sevuvchi, ekologik ongli.


SO'ROVNOMA (o'zingiz haqingizda -
to'g'ri javob yo'q):

  1 eski gazeta va butilkalar:

  5 £1,000: a mo'yna palto  b safari
    c delfinni 'asrab olish'


KALIT:
  ko'proq a → 'yashil' emassiz!
  ko'proq b → harakat qilyapsiz,
    lekin har doim to'g'ri emas
  ko'proq c → Barakalla! Chindan
    'yashil'siz!


⚠ 'A PAVEMENT':

  = yo'lak (piyodalar yo'li).
  ⚠ AmE 'sidewalk'.


⚠ 'TO OFFER':

  = taklif qilmoq (bermoq).
  ⚠ 'offered to give' = berishni
  taklif qildi.


⚠ 'A GIFT' = 'A PRESENT':

  = sovg'a.


⚠ 'A FUR COAT':

  = mo'yna palto.
  ⚠ 'fur' = mo'yna.


⚠ 'TO ADOPT':

  = asrab olmoq.
  ⚠ 'adopt a dolphin' = delfinni
  himoya qilish uchun pul berish.


⚠ 'TO LOOK AFTER':

  = g'amxo'rlik qilmoq, qaramoq.


⚠ 'BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE':

  = juda kech bo'lishidan oldin.


⚠ 'TO GET IT RIGHT':

  = to'g'ri qilmoq.


⚠ 'THINK BEFORE YOU ACT':

  = harakat qilishdan oldin o'yla.
  ⚠ 'to act' = harakat qilmoq.


⚠ 'YOU'RE NOT VERY GREEN, ARE YOU?':

  = savol-quyruq (tag question).
  Inkor gap → ijobiy quyruq.
examples: 1 If you had a lot of old newspapers and empty bottles, would you ... a) leave them on the pavement? b) put them in a rubbish bin? c) recycle them?
2 If somebody offered to give you one of the following as a gift, which would you choose? a) a big, fast car b) a motorbike c) a bicycle
3 If you were in the middle of a city and wanted to go somewhere one or two kilometres away, would you ... a) take a taxi? b) take a bus? c) walk/cycle?
4 If you had a picnic on the beach, what would you do with your rubbish? Would you ... a) leave your rubbish on the beach? b) put your rubbish in the first bin you found? c) take your rubbish home?
5 If you had £1,000 to spend, would you ... a) buy a fur coat? b) go on a safari? c) adopt a dolphin?
Mostly a's: You're not very green, are you? Please look after our world before it's too late!
Mostly b's: You're trying to be more green, but you don't always get it right. Learn more about the environment and think before you act.
Mostly c's: Well done! You're really green! We need more people like you to help us save our environment!

topics.topic: Relative Pronouns - Relative Adverbs — Nisbiy olmoshlar - Nisbiy ravishlar
topics.rule_uz:
NISBIY OLMOShLAR - IKKI GAPNI
  BIRLAShTIRADI.

  I met a woman. She's from
  France.
  → I met a woman WHO is from
    France.
  (qaysi ayol? - Fransiyadan
  bo'lgan)

  WHO   → ODAM:
    A porter is someone WHO
    carries luggage.
  WHICH → NARSA / HAYVON:
    A clock is something WHICH
    shows the time.
  WHERE → JOY (nisbiy ravish):
    This is the hotel WHERE we
    spent our holidays.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Nisbiy gap o'zbekchada '-gan'
  sifatdosh bilan beriladi: 'yuk
  ko'taradigan odam', 'ta'tilni
  o'tkazgan mehmonxona'.


⚠ 'A PORTER':

  = yuk tashuvchi (mehmonxona,
  vokzal).
examples: I met a woman. She's from France. → I met a woman who is from France.
A porter is someone who carries luggage. (who = people)
A clock is something which shows the time. (which = objects / animals)
This is the hotel where we spent our holidays. (where = place)

topics.topic: Some - Any - No / Someone - Something - Somewhere
topics.rule_uz:
SOME / ANY / NO.

  TASDIQ:  SOME  - She's got SOME
           bread.
  SAVOL:   ANY   - Have you got
           ANY milk?
  INKOR:   NOT ANY = NO
           They haven't got ANY
           money. = They've got NO
           money.

  ⚠ Taklif/so'rovda SOME (savol
  bo'lsa ham): Would you like SOME
  more juice?


HOSILALARI (jadval):

            TASDIQ     SAVOL/INKOR  INKOR
  ODAM:     someone    anyone       no one
            somebody   anybody      nobody
  NARSA:    something  anything     nothing
  JOY:      somewhere  anywhere     nowhere

  There is SOMEONE in the kitchen.
  Is there ANYTHING in the box?
  There isn't ANYBODY in the room.
  = There is NOBODY in the room.

  ⚠ 'nobody / nothing / nowhere'
  bilan fe'l TASDIQDA (is, not
  isn't): 'There ISN'T nobody' ✗.


⚠ Who? → someone / anyone / no one
  What? → something / anything /
    nothing
  Where? → somewhere / anywhere /
    nowhere
examples: She's got some bread. (= a little) She's got some pencils. (= a few) — positive statements
Would you like some more orange juice? (offer)
Have you got any milk? No, I haven't got any sugar. (any - questions; not any - negations)
They haven't got any money. = They've got no money.
There is someone in the kitchen. (positive) — Is there anything in the box? There isn't anybody in the room. (questions / negations)
There isn't anybody in the garden. = There is nobody in the garden.
Who? someone / anyone / no one; What? something / anything / nothing; Where? somewhere / anywhere / nowhere
topics.source: Grammar 2, 58-bet (Some - Any - No / Someone - Something - Somewhere)

topics.topic: Grammar: Who - Where - Which — Grammatika: Who - Where - Which
topics.rule_uz:
NISBIY OLMOShLAR - IKKI GAPNI
BIRLAShTIRISh.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  WHO - ODAMLAR                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  I spoke to a policeman. HE was
  very helpful.
  → I spoke to a policeman WHO was
    very helpful.
  ⚠ 'who' = 'he/she/they' o'rnida.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  WHERE - JOYLAR                  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  I went to Spain. I met my husband
  THERE.
  → I went to Spain WHERE I met my
    husband.
  ⚠ 'where' = 'there' o'rnida.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  WHICH - NARSALAR/HAYVONLAR      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  A CD player is a machine. IT
  plays music.
  → A CD player is a machine WHICH
    plays music.
  ⚠ 'which' = 'it' o'rnida.


⚠ 'THAT':

  'who' va 'which' o'rnida 'that'
  ham ishlatiladi (so'zlashuvda):
  'a machine THAT plays music'.


⚠ 'HELPFUL':

  = yordamchan, foydali.
examples: I spoke to a policeman. He was very helpful. → I spoke to a policeman who was very helpful.
I went to Spain. I met my husband there. → I went to Spain where I met my husband.
A CD player is a machine. It plays music. → A CD player is a machine which plays music.

topics.topic: The Infinitive — Infinitiv
topics.rule_uz:
INFINITIV - FE'LNING ASOSIY ShAKLI.

  IKKI XIL:
  a) TO-INFINITIV: to go, to play
  b) TO SIZ: go, play


TO-INFINITIV QAChON:

  1) decide, want, agree, begin,
     refuse, expect dan keyin:
     He wanted TO BUY some sugar.
  2) would like / would love:
     I would like TO HAVE a
     sandwich.


TO SIZ INFINITIV QAChON:

  1) MAKE + kim + fe'l:
     The clown MADE the children
     LAUGH. (kuldirdi)
     My mother MADE me CLEAN my
     room. (majbur qildi)
  2) LET + kim + fe'l:
     My father LETS me USE his
     computer. (ruxsat beradi)
  3) MODAL fe'llar:
     He CAN PLAY tennis well.

  ⚠ 'made me TO clean' ✗, 'can TO
  play' ✗ - to YO'Q!


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  to-infinitiv = '-moq' / '-ish':
  'sotib olmoqchi', 'ishlashni'.
examples: He wanted to buy some sugar. I would like a sandwich. (to-infinitive after decide, want, agree, begin, would like, would love)
The clown made the children laugh. My mother made me clean my room. (infinitive without to after make)
My father lets me use his computer. (after let)
He can play tennis well. (after modal verbs)

topics.topic: The -ing form — -ing shakli
topics.rule_uz:
-ING ShAKLI = FE'L + -ING
  (fishing, watching).

  QAChON:
  1) love, like, hate, enjoy:
     Tom LIKES PLAYING basketball.
  2) don't mind, couldn't help,
     can't stand, look forward to:
     I DON'T MIND GOING shopping.


⚠ 'DON'T MIND':

  = qarshi emasman.


⚠ 'COULDN'T HELP':

  = ... masdan turolmadim.


⚠ 'CAN'T STAND':

  = chiday olmayman.


⚠ 'LOOK FORWARD TO' + -ING:

  bu yerdagi 'to' - predlog, shuning
  uchun -ing: 'look forward to
  SEEING you'.
examples: Tom likes playing basketball in his free time. (after love, like, hate, enjoy)
I don't mind going shopping. (after don't mind, couldn't help, can't stand, look forward to)

topics.topic: Stop - Remember - Forget — Stop - Remember - Forget (ma'no farqi)
topics.rule_uz:
STOP / REMEMBER / FORGET - IKKI
  MA'NO!

  STOP:
  + TO = boshqa ish uchun to'xtadi
    I stopped TO HAVE a coffee.
    (qahva ichgani to'xtadim)
  + -ING = tashladi, tugatdi
    We stopped READING.
    (o'qishni to'xtatdik)

  REMEMBER:
  + TO = unutma (kelajakdagi ish)
    Remember TO BUY milk.
    (sut olishni unutma)
  + -ING = eslayman (o'tgan ish)
    I remember GIVING you the key.
    (kalit berganimni eslayman)

  FORGET:
  + TO = unutdi (qilmadi)
    She forgot TO PAY the bill.
    (to'lashni unutdi)
  + -ING = hech unutmayman
    (qilganimni)
    I'll never forget LEARNING to
    ride a bicycle.

  ⚠ QOIDA: TO = kelajak/keyin;
  -ING = o'tmish/oldin.


JADVAL:

  TO-INFINITIV: decide, want,
    would like/love, begin, refuse,
    agree, expect sb
  TO SIZ: make, let, can, could,
    will, would, may, must
  -ING: love, like, hate, enjoy,
    don't mind, couldn't help,
    can't stand, look forward to
  IKKALASI: stop, remember, forget
examples: I stopped to have a cup of coffee. (stop briefly to do something else) — We stopped reading when the bell rang. (finish, give up)
Please remember to buy some milk. (not forget) — I remember giving you the key before I left. (bring to your mind)
She forgot to pay the phone bill. (not remember) — I'll never forget learning how to ride a bicycle. (always remember)
to-infinitive: decide, want, would like, would love, begin, refuse, agree, expect sb
infinitive without to: make, let, can, could, will, would, may, must
-ing form: love, like, hate, enjoy, don't mind, couldn't help, can't stand, look forward to

INFINITIV yoki -ING? - JADVAL.
